notes: Object insert through includes_element (inverse in_group). 'In which group is calvennium?' reads as the periodic-table group of the family it belongs to (relation in_periodic_group). The s-orbital fact is a firm rule over the family's members. The worlds only differ on fol queries, so they carry no axioms. Relations once declared in this file are catalogued in RELATIONS.md since 2026-10-30.

background.alkali_s: in_group value alkali_metals ⊑ outer_electron_in value s_orbital

queries.not_checked: fol (arithmetic): counts the members of a collection
fol (arithmetic): compares atomic numbers to find the heaviest member

fol.notes: Elements are an enumeration with other_element for any further one; the closed list is a presupposition. 'Heaviest' is read, as the record does, as the highest atomic number. w1 stores the count and the heaviest member as summary facts; w2 stores the rules that read both off the list. heaviest is local.

local.heaviest: heaviest(f): the member of a family of elements with the highest atomic number (an individual, not a value)

alkali_list.says: The alkali metals are lithium, sodium, potassium, rubidium, caesium and francium. (stored)

no_other_alkali.says: No alkali metal is missing from the named ones. (closed list)

stores: number_of_members(alkali_metals) == count(includes_element(alkali_metals, lithium), includes_element(alkali_metals, sodium), includes_element(alkali_metals, potassium), includes_element(alkali_metals, rubidium), includes_element(alkali_metals, caesium), includes_element(alkali_metals, francium), includes_element(alkali_metals, calvennium), includes_element(alkali_metals, other_element))
ForAll(e, Implies(And(includes_element(alkali_metals, e), e != heaviest(alkali_metals)), atomic_number(heaviest(alkali_metals)) > atomic_number(e)))
